name: Carrell Moto Classic
description:
A proper motorcycle jacket in full-grain synthetic bovine leather — the kind that breaks in over years and smells like machine oil and rain. Asymmetric zip closure, snap-down lapels, two chest pockets and a zippered utility pocket on the left sleeve. The shoulders are pre-shaped with a slight forward roll that looks natural on almost any frame. Available in black, oxblood, and a dark tobacco brown that ages beautifully.

Carrell has been making this jacket in essentially the same pattern since 2140. It's not fashionable in any particular direction — it simply exists as a correct object. You see it on Shelf riders who've saved up for months, on Tier 3 commuters who've owned theirs for a decade, on the occasional Tier 4 person who wants something that doesn't look like money.
what_it_says: You bought something once and intend to keep it. You know the difference between a real jacket and a fashion jacket.
worn_by: anyone who wants a jacket that lasts
story_hooks: A jacket passed down from a dead courier contains a hidden interior pocket sewn shut — something is inside.
Carrell has quietly discontinued this model; the remaining stock is being bought up by someone, systematically, across every outlet in the Tier 2 corridor.
The tobacco brown colorway was a limited dye lot from a single supplier who has since vanished — jackets in that color are becoming collector's items on the secondary market.
